title: What is a CPU?
alt: Simple diagram of a CPU connected to computer parts.
simple: The CPU is the computer's main worker. It reads instructions and tells the other parts what to do.
why: FixPilot checks CPU activity and temperature because a busy or overheated CPU can make a computer slow or unstable.
deeper: Think of it as a kitchen chef. A faster chef can prepare more orders, but a chef working in a hot crowded kitchen may need to slow down.
suggestions: Why does a CPU get hot?

title: What is RAM?
alt: Simple desk analogy diagram for RAM working memory.
simple: RAM is your device's short-term working memory. It holds the things you are using right now.
why: When RAM is nearly full, there is less working room. Apps can become slower or may close unexpectedly.
deeper: RAM is like a desk. A larger desk lets you keep more books open at once. Storage is different: it is more like a filing cabinet.
suggestions: What happens when RAM is full?
How can I reduce memory use?

title: What is storage?
alt: Simple diagram of a device saving files to storage.
simple: Storage is where your device keeps files, apps, photos, and games even after it is switched off.
why: Very low free space or an unhealthy drive can cause slow loading, failed updates, and crashes.
deeper: An SSD is usually quicker because it has no moving parts. An HDD uses a spinning disk, more like a tiny record player.
suggestions: How do I check drive health?

title: Why devices need cooling
alt: Simple airflow diagram showing a fan moving heat away from a component.
simple: Working parts create heat. Cooling moves that heat away so the device can keep working safely.
why: FixPilot checks heat because a hot device may deliberately slow down, shut off, or become less reliable.
deeper: Cooling is like opening a window in a warm room. Airflow, clean vents, and a working fan help heat leave instead of building up.

title: What does a router do?
alt: Simple diagram of a router connecting devices to the internet.
simple: A router is the traffic director for your home network. It connects your devices to each other and to the internet.
why: FixPilot checks router symptoms because one unstable router can affect every device connected to it.
deeper: The modem brings the internet service into your home. The router shares that connection with phones, computers, and other devices.
suggestions: How can I improve Wi-Fi coverage?

title: What is DNS?
alt: Simple diagram showing a website name being matched to an IP address.
simple: DNS is like the internet's phone book. It finds the number your device needs when you type a website name.
why: A DNS problem can make websites look broken even when your Wi-Fi connection is working.
deeper: You type a name such as example.com. DNS looks up its IP address, which is the numerical address computers use to find it.
suggestions: Why do some websites not load?

title: How Wi-Fi reaches your device
alt: Simple diagram of Wi-Fi waves weakening through a wall.
simple: Wi-Fi uses radio waves. Distance, walls, and other signals can make those waves weaker.
why: Weak signal can lead to slow speed, high ping, and dropped connections even if your internet plan is fine.
deeper: Ethernet uses a cable, so it is usually steadier. Wi-Fi is more convenient, but it has to travel through the air.
suggestions: Where should I place my router?

title: How a device battery works
alt: Simple battery diagram showing stored energy powering a phone.
simple: A battery stores energy and slowly releases it so your device can run without being plugged in.
why: FixPilot checks battery health and drain because older batteries store less energy and may run down more quickly.
deeper: Every charge cycle adds a little wear. Heat can speed up that wear, which is why battery temperature matters too.
suggestions: Why is my battery draining fast?
Why does heat affect a battery?

title: How charging reaches your device
alt: Simple diagram of a wall adapter, cable, and device charging port.
simple: Charging needs a safe path from the wall adapter, through the cable, into the device's charging port.
why: A damaged cable, weak adapter, or loose port can slow charging or stop it completely.
deeper: Wattage describes how much power a charger can provide. Your device only takes the amount it can safely use.
suggestions: How do I check a charging cable?

title: What updates and drivers do
alt: Simple diagram showing a device receiving a software update.
simple: Updates improve the software on your device. Drivers are small programs that help the operating system talk to hardware.
why: A missing, old, or recently changed driver can affect performance, displays, sound, and network connections.
deeper: Think of a driver as an interpreter between your computer and a specific part, such as a graphics card or Wi-Fi adapter.
suggestions: Can an update cause a problem?

title: How power reaches a device
alt: Simple diagram of electricity moving from an outlet through a power supply to a device.
simple: Power needs a safe, steady path from the outlet to your device. The power supply changes it into the form the device can use.
why: FixPilot checks power symptoms because unstable power can cause restarts, shutdowns, or damage.
deeper: Voltage is like electrical pressure. A surge is a sudden jump in that pressure, which is why surge protection can matter.

title: How a car's main systems work together
alt: Simple car diagram identifying battery, engine, cooling, and brakes.
simple: Your car needs electrical power to start, an engine to move, cooling to control heat, and brakes to stop safely.
why: FixPilot groups these symptoms because one warning sign can help narrow down which system needs attention.
deeper: A warning light is a signal, not a full diagnosis. Repeated warnings, overheating, or reduced braking should be checked promptly.
suggestions: Why is my check-engine light on?
